proposal: The Mandate recommends returning to prior policy by implementing an industry-recognized apprenticeship program (IRAP) separate from the Registered Apprenticeship Program, exploring how to modernize, streamline and remove duplication in the registered program, and asking Congress to re-create the IRAP system by statute so that trade associations and educational institutions can recognize and oversee apprenticeships. It also urges DOL and the NLRB to make it easier for religious organizations to take part in apprenticeship programs.
remaining: A DOL rule or program that recognizes industry-driven apprenticeships separately from Registered Apprenticeship (the 2020 IRAP model), or a statute re-creating it; none was found, and no bill was identified in the one web search run.
Publication of the final registered apprenticeship nondiscrimination rule; it was proposed 2025-07-02 and listed for August 2026 but not found published by 2026-10-07.
Published results of the 120-day plan under EO 14278 and progress toward 1 million new active apprentices; no count was found.
Specific DOL or NLRB steps to facilitate religious organizations' participation in apprenticeship programs; none was found.

status_summary: No revival of industry-recognized apprenticeship programs was found; the administration's actions have centered on the registered program. Executive Order 14278 (signed 2025-04-23) ordered a plan to reach and surpass 1 million new active apprentices, including by extending Registered Apprenticeship to new industries, and does not mention industry-recognized programs. DOL proposed on 2025-07-02 to rescind the affirmative action program requirements of the registered program's equal-opportunity rules and to refer discrimination complaints to enforcement agencies, citing burdens that deter employers from registering programs; DOL's August 2026 regulatory agenda lists the rulemaking, and no final rule had appeared in the Federal Register as of 2026-10-07. A trade article reports DOL awarded $84 million in apprenticeship grants to all states and territories around June 2025. At her confirmation hearing the Labor Secretary nominee said discussions about industry-recognized programs had not yet taken place, per a trade news report. No step to help religious organizations take part was found.

timeline.event: A community college trade publication reports that Labor Secretary nominee Lori Chavez-DeRemer, at her Senate confirmation hearing, committed to strengthening registered apprenticeships and said discussions about industry-recognized programs had not yet taken place (the article date is used; the hearing date is not stated).

President signs EO 14278, Preparing Americans for High-Paying Skilled Trade Jobs of the Future (published 2025-04-28). Section 4 directs the Secretaries of Labor, Commerce and Education to produce a plan within 120 days to reach and surpass 1 million new active apprentices, including extending Registered Apprenticeship to new industries; section 3 orders a review of federal workforce programs. The order does not mention industry-recognized apprenticeships.

According to ACHR News, which cites a DOL release of 2025-06-30, DOL awards $84 million in apprenticeship grants to every state and territory for starting programs, modernizing training and recruiting apprentices.

DOL's Employment and Training Administration proposes Prohibiting Illegal Discrimination in Registered Apprenticeship Programs (90 FR 28947; RIN 1205-AC21). It would rescind the affirmative action program provisions of 29 CFR part 30, including utilization analyses and goals, and refer discrimination complaints to the EEOC or state agencies; DOL says the burdens deter employers, especially small businesses, from registering programs. Comments closed 2025-09-02 (382 comments).

DOL's regulatory agenda lists the registered apprenticeship nondiscrimination rule at the final rule stage with a final rule date of August 2026. A Federal Register search of DOL documents through 2026-10-07 found no final rule.

title: Re-create industry-recognized apprenticeships and streamline Registered Apprenticeship
uncertainties: The absence of an IRAP revival rests on Federal Register searches for 'industry-recognized apprenticeship' (zero results since 2025-01-20), the text of EO 14278, DOL's regulatory agenda, one web search and two trade articles; DOL's own apprenticeship webpages and the 120-day plan were not located, and Congress.gov was not searched for IRAP bills. The $84 million grants and 290,000 registrations are secondary reports (the Secretary's claim as relayed by ACHR News) and were not checked against DOL releases; the ACHR article date is approximated at 2026-02-01. The final-rule status relies on Federal Register searches through 2026-10-07 and could miss a rule published very recently or sent to OIRA. The Mandate's interest in religious organizations' participation has no identified government action. Whether the proposed part 30 rule counts as the 'streamline Registered Apprenticeship' half of the recommendation is a judgment: it removes compliance requirements but was framed by DOL around nondiscrimination law, not duplication.
